prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematical analysis (trigonometry, algebraic equations, function studies, rudiments of differential and integral calculus)

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of the principles and phenomena of microeconomics and macroeconomics.
Knowledge of the main organizational models and legal forms of business.
Knowledge of business accounting documents and basic quantitative tools to evaluate the impact of business decisions.
Ability to interpret the economic context in which the company operates and to predict the effects of business decisions.
Ability to use basic tools for economic-financial analysis of business decisions and for interpreting results.
Autonomy of judgment: Analysis and evaluation of the characteristics of economic systems and the business system, and interpretation of results.
Communication skills: Acquisition and use of the lexicon of economics and business organization.
Learning ability: Ability to autonomously understand and adopt further models and tools for business management.

syllabus_topics: Elements of Economics (Microeconomics: general concepts and theory of supply and demand. Macroeconomics: income circuit and GDP)
The Enterprise (Legal nature of the enterprise. Principles of organizational design)
General accounting. Basics of industrial accounting. Basics of investment analysis
Basics of Project Management (Work Breakdown Structure. Gantt chart. Network techniques)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (open-ended questions and numerical exercises)

assessment_rules: The assessment covers all program topics, requiring demonstration of knowledge and the ability to apply tools and techniques, showing mastery of lexicon and technical terminology. The exam is a single written test, lasting 60 to 90 minutes, composed of open-ended questions and numerical exercises. Minimum requirements for passing are the ability to solve simple exercises on company balance sheet content and basic knowledge of economic systems and organizations. The minimum passing grade is 18/30. Students demonstrating excellent knowledge and high application skills will receive 30/30, and may receive honors if they can apply knowledge and skills in contexts different from those presented in class. There are eight exam sessions per academic year.
